$comment: Written reasons for the capabilities catalogue (docs/DSL_CAPABILITIES.html), batch 12 (the last), 2026-11-24 (REG-357: the owner ordered the rest finished in one go). One reason per keyword: what need it serves and why a lower rung of the extension ladder (expression, function, flow step, hand-written code) or an existing keyword cannot do it. The reasons state the need, not the evidence counts: the catalogue's own columns show samples, tests and examples and change as the corpus grows, so a count written here would go stale. Key = slot id exactly as the catalogue shows it; the generator refuses a reason for a keyword the schema does not have.

reasons.agentAccessExposure.description: An AI agent that may read a concept needs to know in plain words what it holds, such as pizza ingredients and their stock; the hint is shown to the AI with the tool, so it picks the right one without the author writing a prompt somewhere else.
reasons.agentAccessExposure.flow: An agent should be able to act as well as read, for example to place an order; naming a flow offers it to the agent as a tool, so the agent acts through the same checked flow a screen would use and not through a back door.
reasons.aggregateBalance.message: When a balance rule fails, such as more stock leaving than arriving, the person needs a sentence in business words; the template uses the shortfall and the group fields as tokens and defaults to a message built from the rule's name and the shortfall, so the refusal says which group is short and by how much.
reasons.aggregateBalance.rightValue: A balance rule compares two sides of one collection, such as origin and destination quantities; the right value is the marker that identifies the destination side and must differ from the left one, so the two sides are told apart without two collections.
reasons.aggregateCollection.collections: An order has lines and each line may have positions, such as batches or serial numbers; nested collections declare that second level inside the aggregate, so the whole tree is saved and loaded as one unit.
reasons.aggregateCollection.lookupFields: A line often needs a figure that is not stored with it, such as the largest quantity still available; lookup fields attach read-only values from a declared query to every loaded row and are left out of the saved payload, so display data never leaks into stored data.
reasons.autoPanel.transaction: The generated admin block of a concept can include a transaction surface, the aggregate workbench, with settings of its own; this holds those settings for that surface only, so the workbench can be tuned without touching the other generated surfaces.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.computed: A generated table sometimes needs one more read-only column, such as a line total; each computed column is a name and an expression evaluated live, so a simple derived column needs no hand-declared panel.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.dataSource: A generated selection list is built from a default row source that is sometimes wrong, for example showing inactive customers; this replaces that source with a declared one, so the surface stays generated and only its rows change.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.metadata: Tools and reviewers sometimes need a note on a generated surface that no behaviour reads; this free-form object is carried into the compiled model unchanged, so such notes travel with the model without becoming new keywords.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.visibleWhen: Part of a transaction screen should hide in some states, such as the lines of a cancelled order; typed predicates keyed by collection or band name show or hide the region, for presentation only, since hidden rows still commit unchanged, so the screen adapts without risking data.
reasons.capability.operations: A capability is only useful through the operations that flows may call, such as send or findById; the list names them, each a bare name or a full contract with input, output, policy and errors, so a flow can call nothing the capability did not declare.
reasons.capabilityContractSchemaRef.schemaRef: An operation's input or output may be the shape of a declared schema; schemaRef names it, so the contract reuses one definition instead of repeating its fields.
reasons.capabilityOperation.auth: Some operations, such as saving, must be limited to certain people; auth names the roles and scopes a caller must hold, so the limit is checked before the adapter runs and is not left to each flow.
reasons.capabilityOperation.policy: A call to an outside system fails sometimes; the policy states retries, timeout, circuit breaker, bulkhead and idempotency for the operation, so resilience is declared once and not rebuilt in every flow that calls it.
reasons.capabilityPolicy.timeoutMs: A call that never returns would hold a flow forever; the timeout abandons it after the given milliseconds, so a slow outside service fails fast and the flow can handle the failure.
reasons.cellGrid.defaultCols: A board such as a seating plan has a number of columns the data may not state; the default column count applies when the columns field is absent or empty, ten if not set, so a board always has a width.
reasons.cellGrid.palette: A board where a person paints cells needs to know what can be painted; the palette names the query that supplies the paintable values and how each one shows, so the choices come from data and not from the screen's code.
reasons.cellGrid.rowField: A cell board stores one row per cell; the row field names the integer field that holds the cell's zero-based row, so each stored cell lands in the right place on the grid.
reasons.concept.temporal: Prices, tax rates and assignments change over time, and several rows exist for the same thing, each valid in its own window; marking the concept temporal, with its own validFrom and validTo fields, tells the platform the rows are effective-dated windows, so the price on a given day is a rule and not a convention.
reasons.concept.uid: Renaming a concept would look like dropping a table and creating another; a stable identity, generated once and never reused, lets the platform recognise the same concept under a new name, so the rename needs no renamedFrom note and the data follows it.
reasons.context.physicallyIsolate: Some parts of an app, such as payroll, must not share storage with the rest, for legal or safety reasons; the flag stores that context's data apart, so the separation is a property of the model and not a convention of the team.
reasons.conversion.op: A data migration is almost always one of a few moves: copy, split, look up, merge, convert a type, take the first non-empty value, or map literal values; the closed list lets the platform generate and check the step, so the author writes no SQL and a typo is a named error.
reasons.conversionSplitTarget.field: Splitting one old field into several, such as a full name into first and last, must say where each part goes; the target field names the field that receives a part, so the split reads straight from the model.
reasons.documentBand.kind: A printed document has a header with fields of the root and a table of line items; the kind says which a band is, so each band reads the right data.
reasons.enumOption.value: A choice needs a stored value that never changes while its label may; the value is that stored code, so data and rules keep working when the wording changes.
reasons.event.mode: Many events only say that a record was created, updated or deleted; setting the mode on a concept's event makes generated CRUD publish it directly from that mutation, so no flow is needed just to announce a change.
reasons.externalAi.egress: An app that handles sensitive data must control whether anything may leave for an AI vendor; the three levels are no egress, packs built and reviewed locally but never auto-sent, and calls through the vendor adapter, so the app's data policy is declared and checked and not assumed.
reasons.field.access: Some fields, such as a salary or a cost price, should be seen or edited only by some people even on a row they may open; per-field read and write expressions, evaluated per record with the user's identity, add that third level after role and row scope, so field privacy needs no hand-written filter.
reasons.field.default: A new record often should start with a value, such as a status or a quantity of one; the literal is stored when the caller sends none on create, so every creator gets the same starting value.
reasons.field.maxItems: A list field, such as phone numbers, may need a ceiling; the maximum number of elements is checked at the boundary, so no caller can store an oversized list.
reasons.field.minItems: A list field, such as the lines of an order, may need at least some elements; the minimum is checked at the boundary, so an empty list is refused before any rule runs.
reasons.field.sensitive: A field such as a tax id must never reach an outside AI or an unauthorised reader; marking it sensitive redacts it from review packs by field name and omits it from generated reads unless a rule grants access, so protection is on by declaration and errs toward hiding.
reasons.field.uid: Renaming a field would look like dropping a column and adding another; a stable identity, generated once and never reused, lets the platform recognise the same field under a new name, so the rename needs no renamedFrom note and the values follow it.
reasons.flow.startEndpoint: A flow may need an HTTP address that starts it, such as the backend of a button; the flag says whether the generated app offers that start address, and who may start the flow is controlled by expose, so exposing an entry is a decision in the model.
reasons.flowInput.concept: A flow that works on a record should take the record's shape as input; the concept names whose request body the input mirrors, so the flow's contract follows the concept.
reasons.flowStep.name: Every step must be findable in traces and by a hook; the name is unique within the flow, shown in traces and used by a hook's target step, so a step can be told apart without relying on its position.
reasons.guidePageGadget.query: A KPI, a chart or a table on a guide page shows figures; the query names where they come from, so the page reads declared data and holds no hand-written fetch.
reasons.httpConnectorAuth.usernameEnvVar: Some outside services use a username and a password; the username is read from a named environment variable at call time, so no credential appears in the model and each deployment supplies its own.
reasons.httpConnectorOperation.params: An outside call takes values such as an order id placed in the path or the query; the params list names the arguments in the order the caller passes them, and every placeholder used in the operation must be listed, so a call cannot refer to a value that was never bound.
reasons.index.name: An index sometimes needs a chosen name, for a database tool or an operations runbook; the name is generated from the concept and fields when omitted, so the common case needs nothing and the rare one can be pinned.
reasons.lifecycle.transitions: A status field is only trustworthy if the moves are limited; the transitions list the allowed moves, at least one, and a move not listed is refused, so an illegal jump such as reopening a closed order cannot happen from any caller.
reasons.lifecycleState.value: A state needs a stored identity that is also a member of the status field; the value is that code, so transitions and rules refer to a state by one name.
reasons.pack:flows: A pack that offers a feature, such as approval, must bring the flows that run it; listing them in the pack, declared in place or from a model file, installs them with the feature, so each app does not rebuild them.
reasons.panelAction.enabledWhen: A button such as Approve should be clickable only in the right situation; an expression over the record keeps it disabled until the condition is true, so the screen guides the person without a script.
reasons.panelAction.label: A button needs a caption a person reads in their own language; the label is a plain string or one per language, so the caption changes without touching the action's name.
reasons.panelDataSource.procedure: A table sometimes needs rows that no single query returns, such as a merged feed; naming a procedure or a flow replaces the row source entirely with its output, so unusual data needs no special screen.
reasons.panelDataSource.query: A table needs its rows from somewhere; naming a query makes the panel read them from it, so the data is declared once in the query and shared with every other screen that uses it.
reasons.panelLayout.children: A screen may need a table on the left and a form on the right, each possibly split again; nested layouts place the parts inside one another, so a complex screen is composed from simple blocks.
reasons.panelWidget.groupBy: A chart of tickets per status needs to know which field supplies the categories; the distinct values of that field become the categories, so one data source serves a chart with no reshaping.
reasons.property.name: A setting such as a tax rate or a base URL needs a name that rules and expressions can use; it is read as $prop.name, so a value is changed in settings and not by editing the rules that use it.
reasons.property.type: A setting must have a known type; a closed set of string, int, boolean, enum and date, with no objects or arrays, means the cascade resolves one typed value per key, so a setting never turns into a hidden blob.
reasons.query.metadata: Tools and reviewers sometimes need a note on a query that no behaviour reads; this free-form object is carried into the compiled model unchanged, so such notes travel with the model without becoming new keywords.
reasons.query.permissionRequirements: A query that reads sensitive data should be restricted; the listed permissions must be held by a caller to run it, so the limit is declared with the query and applies to every screen, flow or agent that uses it.
reasons.queryParameter.type: A query parameter such as a date range must be checked and converted; the type is a field type name such as string, int, date or uuid, so a bad value is refused before it reaches the database.
reasons.referenceDefinition.defaultFilter: A picker for a reference, such as a customer, often should offer only some rows, such as active ones; the predicate restricts the candidates, so the person is offered only valid choices.
reasons.regionMount.cellGrid: A region of the aggregate workbench can render as a board of cells instead of a table; this holds the board's configuration when the region renders as a cell grid, so a seating or shelf plan is declared and not hand-built.
reasons.root:functions: A calculation used in many places, such as a surge multiplier, would be copied everywhere; a named pure function is replaced by its body at compile time and costs nothing at runtime, so the logic lives once and every expression calls it by name.
reasons.root:schemaVersion: A model file must say which container format it follows, so tools can refuse a file they do not understand; the version is always 1.0.0, and tooling checks it before reading the rest.
reasons.root:screens: An app's screens are what people actually use; each is one archetype from a closed set, such as list, detail, form, board, dashboard or workbench, and experiences navigate to them by a unique name, so a screen is chosen from known kinds and not drawn by hand.
reasons.schemaObject.itemIdentityField: A list of items, such as shipment references, needs a way to tell that two items are the same; naming the property that identifies an element works with the duplication policy, so duplicates are found by identity and not by comparing whole objects.
reasons.schemaObject.properties: An object in a boundary schema must say what it contains; a map from property name to its schema describes each part, so nested input is checked as strictly as flat input.
reasons.workbenchBandPicker.filter: A picker inside a workbench band should offer only candidate rows that fit, such as the products of the order's supplier; an AND-composed predicate, which may use the aggregate root's fields, is enforced on the server, so the narrowing cannot be bypassed from the browser.
